title: Enterprise Risk Management and Management Earnings Forecasts
near_miss_reason: time-varying controls in every column. ERM is a binary absorbing firm-specific adoption indicator estimated with gvkey and fyear fixed effects (reghdfe), but Table 4 columns 1-2, Tables 6-9 and the Table 5 eventdd event study all include 9-13 time-varying firm controls ($controls_issuance / $controls_error); Table 10 is a stacked DiD (also with controls). Dropping the controls from Table 4 or Table 5 would yield eligible static TWFE and event-study specifications.
eligible_reason: Staggered binary design: ERM = 1 from the fiscal year a firm adopted enterprise risk management (hand-collected; README states no firm ever discontinued), firms adopt in different years 2002-2022 (share of adopters rises from 3% to 79%; 2001 adopters are dropped), never-adopters remain, and the estimator is linear TWFE with firm and year FE. Fails only on time-varying controls in every reported column, hence near-miss.
design_notes: Firm-fiscal-year panel of firms ever in the S&P 500 (1990-2022), analysis years 2001-2022 (16,077 firm-years in erm_full; Table 2 log). Two analysis files: erm_guid_final.dta (forecast issuance, H1) and erm_error_final.dta (forecast error, H2), both PSM-matched samples after dropping 2001 adopters, missing-control firms and singletons (T1 Panel A/B.do). Table 4 (T4.do lines 14, 20): reghdfe Issuance ERM $controls_issuance, absorb(gvkey fyear) cluster(gvkey); reghdfe Error ERM $controls_error. Table 5 (T5.do lines 12, 18): eventdd with timevar = fyear - ermimpyear, method(hdfe, absorb(gvkey fyear)), baseline(-3) leads(3) lags(4) accum, with controls. Table 6: Earn_Vol on ERM + controls. Tables 7-8: subsample splits (complexity, financial challenge, industry earnings volatility, political risk) with suest tests. Table 9: long vs short horizon error. Table 10: stacked DiD (Barrios toolkit) with cohort x firm and cohort x year FE, controls, +/-3 years, clean controls = never-treated or adopting > 5 years later. Figure 1: gsem mediation paths with firm and year dummies.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Adoption fiscal years 2002-2022 (2001 adopters dropped via missing2001); ERM share by year from the Stata log Table 2: 0.032 (2001) rising to 0.792 (2022), with the largest jump 2009-2010 (0.259 to 0.466, plausibly SEC 2009 risk-oversight disclosure rules). Exact cohort sizes not in the log.
modern_estimators_note: Stacked DiD (Table 10) following Baker-Larcker-Wang / Cengiz et al.; not CSA/BJS/SA/dCDH.

data_access_note: No data files shipped. Raw inputs are WRDS products (Compustat, CRSP, IBES Guidance/Actuals/Summary, BoardEx, Audit Analytics SOX 302/404, Thomson 13f) plus firmlevelrisk.com and the authors' hand-collected ERM adoption file (gvkey, ermever, ermbegin), which is not included. SAS code rebuilds erm_full.dta; Stata code builds erm_guid_final / erm_error_final.
data_files: Stata Log/Statalog.smcl and SAS Logs/*.log (real-data logs)
software_notes: Stata (reghdfe, eventdd, estout, gsem, suest, distinct) and SAS for data construction.
replication_feasible_note: Would require the hand-collected ERM adoption dates from the authors plus WRDS access; and even then no reported column is eligible.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Treatment timing from README (ermbegin) and Table 2 ERM shares in the Stata log. Sample is PSM-matched (allowed as a sample restriction) and singletons are dropped. Baseline for the event study is t = -3 with accumulation.
